queries.query: the raw matter for the alchemists' work, a mineral bred underground in two varieties found across Europe, the finer of which is stamped with the outward shape of the greater world
queries.note: The opening on nature begetting the mineral; 'bowels of the earth', 'eastern part of the sphere of the Sun', 'Southern Star', 'first efflorescence' paraphrased away.

queries.query: the accelerated great work: not nine months but forty days are enough to fix the substance, carry it through putrefaction and fermentation into a stone, and hatch the alchemical phoenix
queries.note: The Spagyric shortcut; 'Sulphur of Cinnabar', 'Flying Eagle whose wings fly away without wind' paraphrased away; forty days and the phoenix kept as reader-honest anchors of the passage.

queries.query: why do so many people seek the great secret and so few ever find it
queries.note: 'What many seek after and few find'; the rarity of true attainment is answered across many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
